title: Barometric Pressure Sensor: 7 Simple Steps to Accurate Data
text:
Pressure

 Barometric Pressure Sensor: 7 Simple Steps to Accurate Data

 Every weather station, drone altimeter and smartphone floor counter depends on a tiny absolute pressure cell that feels the weight of the air above it. This guide explains how that cell works, how its reading becomes altitude and how engineers calibrate it with confidence.

 
 Absolute MEMS Cell 
 hPa and mbar 
 Altitude Formula 
 BMP280 and BMP390 
 




 A barometric pressure sensor measures the absolute pressure of the surrounding air, usually in hPa. With the right formula, careful mounting and periodic calibration it reports weather trends, altitude and an atmospheric reference for gauge pressure.


 
 Hello everyone, today we are going to learn how a barometric pressure sensor works, how it converts air pressure into altitude and how to install and calibrate it correctly.


 
 
 
 What Is a Barometric Pressure Sensor?


 A barometric pressure sensor is an absolute pressure sensor designed to measure the pressure of the surrounding atmosphere, usually between about 300 and 1100 hPa. Unlike a gauge pressure transmitter , it compares the air against a sealed vacuum reference instead of against the atmosphere itself.


 Atmospheric pressure at sea level averages 1013.25 hPa in the standard atmosphere and falls as you climb. The difference between the two reference types is explained in absolute vs gauge pressure , and it is the key to understanding why a barometer needs a sealed cavity.


 
 
 Image credit: AZoM . Illustration courtesy of AZoM, shown here for educational reference. 
 

 AZoM notes that modern barometric sensors can resolve pressure differences as small as 0.01 hPa. The same article explains that most devices use either a capacitive diaphragm or a piezoresistive bridge, followed by built in temperature compensation.


 Do You Know?
 A change of 1 hPa near sea level corresponds to roughly 8 metres of height. That is why a good barometer chip can tell which floor of a building you are standing on.



 
 
 Advertisement 


 
 


 Units You Will Meet: hPa, mbar and Friends


 Meteorologists use hectopascal, and 1 hPa equals exactly 1 mbar or 100 Pa. Older instruments in India still show mmHg or inHg, so a quick atm to kPa pressure conversion table is handy on any instrument bench.


 
 1013.25 hPa Standard sea level pressure 

 760 mmHg Same value in mercury 

 29.92 inHg Aviation altimeter setting 

 1 hPa = 1 mbar Exact unit equivalence 




 Aviation in India uses hPa for the altimeter setting called QNH, while many American products still print inHg. Always check the unit before comparing two barometers.


 How a MEMS Barometric Pressure Sensor Works Inside


 Inside a MEMS barometric pressure sensor sits a thin silicon diaphragm etched over a cavity sealed under vacuum. Air pressure bends the diaphragm, and the bending is sensed either by piezoresistors in a Wheatstone bridge or by a change in capacitance, as compared in piezoresistive vs capacitive pressure sensors .


 
 Air Pressure Atmosphere pushes on the silicon diaphragm

 Diaphragm Bends Vacuum cavity below gives an absolute reference

 Bridge Signal Piezoresistors or capacitance change by microvolts

 ASIC and ADC Signal is amplified and digitised with temperature

 Compensation Stored coefficients correct offset and span

 Digital Output Pressure in Pa sent over I²C or SPI




 The tiny bridge signal goes to an on chip amplifier and a high resolution analog to digital converter . The same silicon micromachining is used in the MEMS accelerometer , which is why these parts are so small and cheap.


 Silicon is strongly temperature sensitive, so every chip includes a temperature sensor and factory trimming coefficients stored in memory. Your firmware reads raw pressure and temperature, then applies the compensation formula from the datasheet, a correction similar to the thermal zero and span shift handling in industrial transmitters.


 Quick Tip
 Always read the temperature register before the pressure register and use the datasheet compensation code exactly. Skipping the temperature step gives errors of several hPa.



 4 Common Sensing Technologies Compared


 
 Piezoresistive MEMS
 Implanted resistors on a silicon diaphragm form a bridge.
 Best for: phones, drones, IoT nodes
 Most common 

 Capacitive MEMS
 Diaphragm and fixed plate form a capacitor that changes with pressure.
 Best for: low power wearables
 Low drift 

 Resonant Silicon
 Pressure changes the frequency of a vibrating silicon beam.
 Best for: reference barometers, aviation
 Very stable 

 Aneroid Capsule
 Sealed metal capsule expands and moves a pointer or LVDT.
 Best for: dial barographs, legacy panels
 Mechanical 




 Industrial transmitters use the same physics on a larger scale, as described in absolute pressure transmitter working principle . Resonant sensors cost much more but hold calibration for years, so national weather networks and calibration labs prefer them.


 BMP280 and BMP390: Two Popular Examples


 
 
 Parameter BMP280 BMP390 

 Pressure range 300 to 1100 hPa 300 to 1250 hPa 

 Relative accuracy ±0.12 hPa, about ±1 m ±0.03 hPa, about ±0.25 m 

 Absolute accuracy ±1 hPa ±0.5 hPa 

 Interfaces I²C and SPI I²C up to 3.4 MHz, SPI up to 10 MHz 

 Package 2.0 × 2.5 mm 2.0 × 2.0 × 0.75 mm 

 



 Bosch Sensortec states in the BMP390 datasheet that relative accuracy is typically ±3 Pa, equivalent to ±0.25 m of height, between 700 and 1100 hPa. The same datasheet gives an absolute accuracy of typically ±50 Pa and a temperature coefficient of offset of ±0.6 Pa per kelvin.


 The BMP390 draws only 3.2 µA at one reading per second in its low power mode, according to Bosch Sensortec. Both chips talk over the buses compared in SPI vs I2C protocol comparison , so any small microcontroller can read them.


 Do You Know?
 The BMP390 package measures only 2.0 by 2.0 by 0.
